page.layout: Marginal notes in one column at the left of the visible strip, from top to bottom: four notes, each set in small type beside the text block. No main text is visible.; One running table in a ruled box: consul names on the left, one year beside each group of names on the right; catchword at the lower right.

note.i: Civitas Groning. socijque in agro pa-cti sunt cum Ulrico de commercijs & usu AMASI fl. Sed pacto plebs oppidana intercessit.
Conventio nova civitatis cum Davide episc. Ultr. de praefectura suburbana: Item cum Hou-werdeis.
Fœdus civitatis cum Upsicranis per-petuum, civitati honorificum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Houwerdeis" in the third note; "Upsicranis" in the fourth note, with the l possibly an i; "AMASI fl." where the abbreviation after AMASI is unclear. The first line of the note block may be set in a slightly larger face, but its letters are clear. The years are printed in old-style numerals (for example 1456 appears as I456 in the scan); they are copied here as Arabic numerals.
